blocks.text: Protecting a Name in the Interpreted Language

The interpreter stores variables and constants as bindings. Each binding adds bool modificable: true allows assignment, while false prevents it. This rule is checked when the interpreter runs; it is not the C++ compiler's const or constexpr declaration. Clients operate only through the Tabla_nombres interface.

The session starts with unidad=1 and limite=100, both constants. They occupy two of the eight entries, leaving six for user-created bindings. We keep integers: limite names the upper bound 100, although the literal 100 is rejected. Every binding value and intermediate result remains within -100..100.

blocks.question: unidad is marked as a constant. Which operation respects the contract?
blocks.explanation: Reading a constant in an expression is valid. Assigning to it is rejected, and so is creating a name that already exists.

blocks.text: Notation for Protected Creation

fija name = expression creates a nonmodifiable binding. crea still creates a modifiable binding. fija is recognized as a reserved word only when the entire name matches; fija2 is a name, and so is Fija. The table rejects crea and fija as binding names. The lexer and token_valido consistently incorporate the new token category.

A user-defined constant requires an initializer and terminator, just like a variable. It may look up previously accepted names. Its value is stored at that moment: fija copia=base+1; is not automatically reevaluated when base changes.

blocks.question: After crea base=3;fija copia=base+1;base=7;, what value does copia retain?
options: Four, computed when its creation was accepted.
Eight, because it stays linked to the initial expression.
Three, because reading base during initialization is not allowed.
blocks.explanation: An int is stored, not a formula or a reference to base's value. Later assignment to base does not recalculate copia.

blocks.text: Check Protection Before Modification

asignar still searches by reference, but it now checks modificable before writing. An absent constant does not exist: there is no special kind of lookup that creates one. definir enforces uniqueness and capacity for both kinds of binding. The candidate copy includes the protection flag, not just the name and value.

blocks.question: Arrange the branch that found the destination binding. Assume the numeric candidate has already passed its range check.
blocks.explanation: A protected binding triggers a diagnostic before writing. The same rule applies to predefined constants and user-defined constants.

blocks.text: The program creates both predefined bindings only once, before the input-reading loop. Resetting the table on every iteration would lose variables from earlier operations. Predefined means available at the start; constant describes a separate protection rule. In this model both predefined bindings are protected.
A Session with States Governed by Different Rules

To display the policy, we use C++'s conditional operator: (condition ? true_text : false_text). It first evaluates the condition and then only the expression in the selected branch. In (dato.modificable ? "(V)" : "(C)"), true selects "(V)" and false selects "(C)"; the parentheses group this selection as the text passed to <<. The operator chooses an output marker: it neither changes the binding nor decides whether an assignment is permitted. That protection is checked separately before writing.

The values 3, 4, 7, 4, and 100 are accepted, while the change to unidad is rejected. base remains seven, copia four, and the predefined bindings retain their values. The final table shows (V) for modifiable and (C) for constant. These markers display the stored policy; they are not part of the input syntax.
Boundary Values and Shared Capacity

blocks.question: Predict the entire output with a constant at the boundary and a rejected assignment.
answers:
Value: -100
Error: Constant name
Value: -1
Value: 1
Accepted: 3
Rejected: 1
Table: unidad=1(C) limite=100(C) borde=-100(C)
blocks.explanation: Creating borde reaches the lower bound. The assignment does not change its value. -100%3 is -1, and unidad remains one.

blocks.question: There are two predefined bindings and six user-created bindings. What should happen to a new constant?
options: Replace unidad to keep eight entries.
Reject it with Table full and preserve all eight bindings.
Accept it because constants do not take up space.
blocks.explanation: Capacity counts every binding. Modification policy does not remove an association from the vector.

blocks.text: Guided Integration: Constants and Rejected Creations

Extend the session with the fija token category and per-binding protection. The initial case is "crea base=4;fija copia=base+2;base=9;copia;limite=3;limite;". It should accept 4, 6, 9, 6, and 100, reject the change to limite, and preserve copia=6. Do not implement protection that is merely visual: asignar must actually reject modification.

Test "fija x=5 2;x;" and confirm that x remains absent; "fija x=unidad;x=x+1;x;" preserves one; "crea unidad=3;unidad;" rejects the duplicate and preserves one; "crea a=limite+1;a;" rejects an out-of-range result and leaves the name absent. Fill the six available slots with distinct names and reject the seventh; then look up an earlier binding again.

Criteria: whole-word recognition and reserved names, copying all protection metadata into the candidate table, initializing predefined values only once, checking protection before writing, sharing capacity, and accepting only after ;. Open the reference only after checking each case and explaining the state that should remain.
Later Reference with a Different State

The reference leaves tramo=8 and sello=5, accepts 2, 5, 8, 5, and 1, and rejects an assignment to a constant. Creating and reading a constant is not the same as assigning to it. The next construction will integrate these rules with history and a summary of accepted state.

The supporting source covers constants and interpreter variables (Stroustrup, 2024, sections 6.8.3–6.8.4 and exercise 3 in chapter 6). The integer predefined names and fija notation belong to this limited model.
